classification.difficultyReason: Match both the cosine amplitude and the line's gradient and intercept to a supplied pair.

content.prompt: Which graph could be used to solve $2\cos x=x-1$?

spec.description: Cosine curve with amplitude 1 and increasing line; labelled option A.
spec.mathematics: y=cos x and y=x-1; horizontal ticks at 1 and pi; vertical ticks at -2, -1, 1 and 2; no grid.

spec.description: Cosine curve with amplitude 2 and decreasing line; labelled option B.
spec.mathematics: y=2 cos x and y=1-x; horizontal ticks at 1 and pi; vertical ticks at -2, -1, 1 and 2; no grid.

spec.description: Cosine curve with amplitude 2 and increasing line; labelled option C.
spec.mathematics: y=2 cos x and y=x-1; horizontal ticks at 1 and pi; vertical ticks at -2, -1, 1 and 2; no grid.

spec.description: Sine curve with amplitude 2 and increasing line; labelled option D.
spec.mathematics: y=2 sin x and y=x-1; horizontal ticks at 1 and pi; vertical ticks at -2, -1, 1 and 2; no grid.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=2\cos x$ and $y=x-1$. The cosine curve has amplitude $2$, so it starts at the maximum $(0,2)$. The line has gradient $1$, vertical intercept $-1$ and horizontal intercept $1$. These are the two graphs shown in C.

Correct answer: C.
